skill.name: technical-drawing
skill.description: Creates precise static technical drawings of physical objects, with coherent views and fine linework. Delivers a blank-page viewer with zoom, editable colors and SVG, PNG and PDF downloads.
skill.summary: Create coherent technical illustrations with editable vector geometry, a standalone viewer, and SVG, PNG, and PDF exports.

content.user_title: Create Technical Drawings With Editable Exports
content.value_statement: Technical illustrations can lose consistency when views, annotations, and exports are created separately. This skill builds shared geometry and packages a local viewer with coordinated downloads.
actual_capabilities: Guide coherent assembled, exploded, orthographic, and section illustrations from shared geometry and documented references.
Construct illustrative mechanical geometry with lathe, extrusion, helix, spring, screw, and knurl helpers.
Project meshes with configurable parallel cameras and sampled hidden-line removal.
Build a standalone viewer with zoom, appearance settings, linework presets, parameter controls, and part selection.
Export SVG, 300 dpi PNG, and vector PDF with selected colors, crop settings, and optional transparent paper.
Provide verification checklists for geometry correspondence, annotations, physical dimensions, and downloaded artifacts.
limitations: Photographs and descriptions do not establish hidden construction, exact dimensions, tolerances, or manufacturing suitability.
Bundled geometry helpers do not provide general CAD booleans, manufacturing thread solids, or arbitrary section cuts.
The viewer builder requires Node.js, authored model scripts, and locally installed PDF and font dependencies.
Visual quality and export behavior require rendering and browser inspection; generated files alone do not prove correctness.

prompt_templates.title: Draw One Referenced Object
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a technical illustration of [object] from [reference]. Use one parallel view, record estimated features, and deliver editable SVG.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an Assembly
prompt_templates.prompt: Create assembled and exploded views of [assembly] using [parts and dimensions]. Keep shared geometry and include a parts list with verified quantities.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Editable Viewer
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a standalone viewer for [object] with [validated parameters], part isolation, line colors, and SVG, PNG, and PDF downloads. Verify matching exports.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Multi-View Technical Sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [authoritative geometry], [units], and [drafting standard] for aligned views and [section plane]. Verify dimensions and exports; report missing evidence before fabrication claims.

output_examples.input: Illustrate a hollow sleeve from supplied dimensions with an editable length control.
output: Standalone sleeve viewer with a validated length control and zoom.
Editable SVG, 300 dpi PNG, and vector PDF exports.
Source model, configuration, dependencies, and stated construction assumptions.

output_examples.input: Explain how a cover, screws, and housing fit together using supplied geometry.
output: Assembled and exploded views generated from one part inventory.
Named component selection, isolation, coloring, and individual SVG download.
Optional annotated sheet with verified item quantities and anchored leaders.

best_practices: Provide authoritative geometry, dimensions, units, intended use, and references before requesting exact or manufacturing-oriented drawings.
Use one model for every view and verify mating features at minimum, default, and maximum parameter values.
Use trusted model scripts, sanitize imported SVG, and inspect the viewer and downloaded files independently.
anti_patterns: Presenting inferred interiors, unknown tolerances, or illustrative threads as verified fabrication geometry.
Drawing each view independently or changing projected ink to conceal assembly misalignment.
Treating a successful build as visual verification or using unsanitized imported SVG in the viewer.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools. File generation and inspection depend on the tools available locally.

faq.question: Can it create manufacturing-ready drawings?
faq.answer: Only established geometry, dimensions, units, fits, and drafting requirements support fabrication claims. Illustrative outputs do not establish manufacturing suitability or standards compliance.

faq.question: Can it reconstruct an object from photographs?
faq.answer: It can guide proportional reconstruction of visible features. Hidden construction and unspecified dimensions must remain omitted, estimated, or explicitly illustrative.

faq.question: Does the standalone viewer work offline?
faq.answer: The builder embeds scripts, PDF libraries, and the font into one HTML file. Install dependencies locally before building and verify offline browser behavior.

faq.question: Which download formats are provided?
faq.answer: The bundled viewer provides editable SVG, 300 dpi PNG, and vector PDF. Downloads use the selected geometry, linework, and colors rather than viewing zoom.

faq.question: What should be trusted before building?
faq.answer: Review model scripts as executable generator source and sanitize imported SVG. The builder reads configured inputs and writes to the specified output path.
